name: ByteNet Orders Withdrawal Button
author: bytenet

sections.description:
ByteNet Orders Withdrawal Button adds a complete withdrawal-request flow to your WooCommerce store:

  • «Withdraw from the contract here» button everywhere: floating button, footer link, “My Account”, order emails, shortcode, and Gutenberg block.
  • 2-step form with the minimum required fields, with an immediate receipt confirmation showing date/time.
  • Works for guests (order number + email) and for logged-in customers.
  • Full request management in wp-admin: filters, search, case detail screen, internal notes, complete history, bulk actions, CSV export (compatible with Greek Excel).
  • Article-16 exclusions per product, with a customer-facing notice that never blocks submission.
  • Optional IBAN field with validity check (MOD-97), encryption, masked display in admin, and logged reveal actions.
  • Two WooCommerce emails (customer + store), with full template override support.
  • GDPR compliance: personal data export/erasure, automatic anonymization, hashed IPs.
  • No request is ever auto-rejected — the deadline estimate is shown only in the admin area.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the bytenet-orders-withdrawal-button folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin from the “Plugins” menu.
  3. Configure it under WooCommerce > Settings > Withdrawal.
  4. Manage requests under WooCommerce > Withdrawal.
sections.faq:
Does the customer need an account?

No. Guests are identified by order number and the order’s email address.

Where is the IBAN stored?

Encrypted in the database. Only the last digits are shown in the admin area; a full reveal is logged in the request’s history.
sections.changelog:
1.8.3

  • Renamed all PHP classes, functions, hooks, option names, meta keys, and the database tables from the short “WB_”/”wb_” prefix to “BYTEORWI_”/”byteorwi_” to avoid collisions, per wordpress.org plugin review feedback. Existing installs are migrated automatically on activation (no data loss).
  • Renamed the [withdrawal_button]/[withdrawal_form] shortcodes to [byteorwi_withdrawal_button]/[byteorwi_withdrawal_form] for the same reason.
  • Text domain changed to match the plugin slug (bytenet-orders-withdrawal-button).
  • Replaced a raw <style> tag with wp_add_inline_style().

1.8.2

  • Fixed remaining phpcs:ignore placement for direct-query/no-caching/unescaped-parameter warnings and normalized file line endings.

1.8.1

  • Fixed placement of phpcs:ignore annotations so Plugin Check no longer flags already-reviewed direct database queries as unprepared SQL.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

short_description: Full implementation of the right of withdrawal (articles 9-16, Greek Law 2251/1994 / EU Directive 2011/83/EU) for WooCommerce stores.
